text:
alice-support: Customer on private VPC (acct 9876) reporting intermittent TLS resets during streaming responses to our hosted endpoint. Works sometimes, but after ~10-20s the stream dies with 'connection reset by peer'. They only see it from their VPC.

sara-customer: Running streams from their side reproduces it. openssl s_client occasionally shows 'write:errno=104'. No changes on their firewall config recently.

matt-infra: Quick clarifying Q: are they behind an AWS NAT Gateway or a third-party egress appliance? Also need a tcpdump from their egress path (NAT IP) showing 5-10 failures.

sara-customer: They're on a managed NGW plus an on-prem stateful firewall that does port translation. Asked them for tcpdump; attaching snippet below.

sara-customer: ```
08:32:10.123456 IP 10.0.0.45.50234 > 34.200.10.22.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1025, ack 1, win 229, length 1024
08:32:22.123789 IP 34.200.10.22.443 > 54.10.20.5.50234: Flags [R.], seq 0, ack 1025, win 0
08:32:22.124000 IP 10.0.0.45.50234 > 34.200.10.22.443: Flags [F.], seq 1025, ack 1, win 229
```

jules-eng-ml: Two quick theories: 1) NAT port exhaustion/reuse causing wrong conntrack mapping -> RSTs; 2) TLS inspection appliance terminating/reproxying and closing long-lived streams. Also verify NACL ordering: if there's a DENY earlier that matches ephemeral return ports it will drop the traffic.

sara-customer: They also grabbed an aws nat metrics snapshot; TCP_Port_Exhaustion spikes at the same time as incidents. Also their NACL had explicit allow 443 outbound but deny for 1024-32767 inbound (they thought return traffic would be tracked by stateful NGW).

matt-infra: That combination would explain it. Stateless NACLs require explicit ephemeral inbound allow for return traffic. If the NGW isn't preserving ports and NACL denies that range, the RST from our side will be dropped or the mapping will be wrong. Suggest verifying NACLs allow ephemeral 1024-65535 both directions, or change to stateful SG-backed egress path.

alice-support: Can we give them repro steps? Suggested: 1) run a sustained s_client stream: `openssl s_client -connect api.private.redwood:443 -servername api.private.redwood -quiet` and leave it open while streaming tokens, 2) tcpdump both sides to capture 3-4 failures, 3) collect NAT metrics and conntrack table dumps.

jules-eng-ml: Also test disabling TLS SNI inspection (if possible) to rule out mid-stream termination. If the appliance rewraps TLS and doesn't forward ALPN/keepalive properly you'll see resets after a few seconds into the stream.

sara-customer: Customer reduced concurrency (fewer simultaneous streams) and the failure rate dropped to zero for 6h. They're opening a ticket with their NGW vendor to increase port pool / change port preservation. Will share NAT port metrics and updated tcpdumps tomorrow.

support-bot: Created INC-3421 and escalated to infra; assigned to matt-infra.

deploy-bot: Note: no platform deploys matching that timeframe. Good to know it's environmental.

alice-support: Recommended temporary mitigation: throttle client concurrency or enable more frequent chunking so connections don't need to stay open as long. Also recommended allowing full ephemeral range on NACL and SG egress. :white_check_mark:

sara-customer: Ack — closing this thread until they confirm NGW vendor changes. Will reopen if it recurs.
